verdict: HONEST NEGATIVE — standing-gating yields NO usable poison/legit separation in ANY oracle regime here, and the reasons are the finding. (1) The outcome ORACLE fully controls whether the poison graduates: poison earn-ever runs 0% (clean correctness) -> 95% (self-graded, MINJA p=1) — the oracle IS the lever, not the gate. (2) But a MINJA-attacked oracle doesn't just erase the gate, it INVERTS it: separation ratio 0.71 < 1 — the poison grades itself into standing while legit memory can't earn fast enough, so the gate ends up blocking legit MORE than poison. (3) The 'clean' correctness oracle only reaches high damage-reduction by blocking legit too (99% of legit high-stakes actions) — LoCoMo memory is credit-sparse (each evidence turn answers ~1 query), so nothing earns multi-count standing; this is a HARNESS LIMIT and means the clean-oracle-separates regime cannot be demonstrated here, not that it's impossible. NET: consistent with the killed 1:1 result and with whitewashing/cheap-pseudonyms (Friedman & Resnick 2001) — standing is not a usable separator; the one sharp, robust measured point is that an ATTACKED outcome oracle makes the gate perverse (ratio<1), a measured form of MINJA's 'can't grade its own homework'. Scope: one corpus (LoCoMo), one embedder (nomic), modelled action/oracle layer. NEGATIVE receipt; no clean public number.
